verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय॥
verses.transliteration:
dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya

translations.english: Dhritarâshtra said: On the holy plain, on the field of Kuru, gathered together, eager for battle, what did they, O Sanjaya, my people and the Pândavas?

explanations.en: The Bhagavad Gita opens with the blind king Dhritarashtra asking his charioteer Sanjaya for news of the battle about to begin between his sons (the Kauravas) and his nephews (the Pandavas). The phrase dharma-kshetre kuru-kshetre — the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus — sets the stage as both a literal battlefield and a metaphor for the inner field of moral conflict. Every verse that follows is Sanjaya's report of what unfolds there.

explanations.en: Krishna draws Arjuna's attention to the nature of sensory experience: it is transient by definition — every pleasure ends, every pain ends. explanations.en: These bodies, occupied by the eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable embodied Self, are described as coming to an end. Therefore fight, O Bharata. Krishna uses the Atman's imperishability as the direct reason for Arjuna to act.

verses.sanskrit:

उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते॥

translations.english: He who regardeth this as a slayer, and he who thinketh he is slain, both of them are ignorant. He slayeth not, nor is he slain.

explanations.en: He who thinks the Self slays and he who thinks the Self is slain both fail to understand. The Self neither slays nor is slain. This is a foundational teaching: agency belongs to nature, not to the Self.

verses.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि
न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥
verses.transliteration:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadāci
nnāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṁ purāṇo
na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre

translations.english: He is not born, nor doth he die; nor having been, ceaseth he any more to be; unborn, perpetual, eternal and ancient, he is not slain when the body is slaughtered.

explanations.en: One of the Gita's clearest statements about the imperishable nature of the Self (atman). The verse strips away every temporal attribute — birth, death, becoming, ending — to point to a layer of being that persists across the changes of the body. It is the metaphysical ground for Krishna's argument that Arjuna's grief over those he is about to fight is rooted in identifying with the perishable rather than the eternal.

explanations.en: Among the most cited verses in the entire Bhagavad Gita. Krishna teaches the principle of nishkama karma — action performed without attachment to its results. तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ॥
verses.transliteration:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau

translations.english: Affection and aversion for the objects of sense abide in the senses; let none come under the dominion of these two; they are obstructors of the path.

explanations.en: In each sense object, attachment and aversion are established. Do not come under the power of either, for they are the obstacles on one's path. These two forces together are the root of bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः॥
verses.transliteration:

svadharme nidhanaṁ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ

translations.english: Better one's own duty, though destitute of merit, than the duty of another, well discharged. Better death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is full of danger.

explanations.en: Better is one's own duty performed imperfectly than the duty of another performed well. Death in one's own duty is better; the duty of another brings danger. The teaching of svadharma (one's own duty) here applies to inner vocation, not merely social role.

explanations.en: Arjuna asks: by what is a person compelled to commit sin against his will, as if driven by force? The question points to the experience everyone knows: doing what one does not want to do.

translations.english: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is wrath, begotten by the quality of motion; all-consuming, all-polluting, know thou this as our foe here on earth.

explanations.en: Krishna answers: it is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion (rajas). Know this to be the great devourer, the great evil here. Desire and anger together are identified as the single source of moral failure.

explanations.en: As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as a womb covers the embryo, so wisdom is covered by this (desire). The three analogies describe three different degrees of concealment.

verses.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः॥

translations.english: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.

explanations.en: The senses are superior to the body. The mind is superior to the senses. The intellect is superior to the mind. That which is superior to even the intellect is the Self. This ascending hierarchy locates the center of the human being.

translations.english: Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;

explanations.en: Krishna introduces the doctrine of avatara — divine descent. The verse pairs with the one that follows to frame divine intervention not as a single event but as an ongoing response woven into the structure of time.

translations.english: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness, I am born from age to age.

translations.english: The four castes were emanated by Me, by the different distribution of qualities and actions; know Me to be the author of them, though the actionless and inexhaustible.

explanations.en: The fourfold order of varna was created by Krishna according to the distinctions of quality and action. Though he is the creator of this order, he is not its agent, being unchangeable and actionless.

verses.sanskrit:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते॥
verses.transliteration:

translations.english: Nor do actions affect Me, nor is the fruit of action desired by Me. He who thus knoweth Me is not bound by actions.

explanations.en: Actions do not taint Krishna because he has no desire for the fruits of actions. One who understands this truly is not bound by action either. The freedom of the knower mirrors the freedom of the Lord.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्॥

translations.english: Having thus known, our forefathers, ever seeking liberation, performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did our forefathers in the olden time.

explanations.en: Ancient seekers of liberation performed action knowing this truth. Therefore Arjuna should also perform action as the ancients performed it in the past. The continuity with tradition is itself a source of authority.

translations.english: "What is action, what inaction"? Even the wise are herein perplexed. Therefore I will declare to thee the action by knowing which thou shalt be loosed from evil.

explanations.en: Even the wise are confused about what is action and what is inaction. Krishna will teach Arjuna about action so that Arjuna may be liberated from evil. The teaching of karma is more subtle than it first appears.

explanations.en: One must understand action (karma), wrong action (vikarma), and inaction (akarma). The nature of action is deep and difficult to understand. These three categories are the subject of the next several verses.

verses.sanskrit:

translations.english: He who seeth inaction in action, and action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is harmonious, even while performing all action.

explanations.en: The one who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise among humans and is a yogi who has accomplished all action. The paradox here is at the heart of karma yoga: acting without acting, from the standpoint of the Self.

येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि॥
verses.transliteration:

translations.english: And having known this, thou shalt not again fall into this confusion, O Pândava; for by this thou wilt see all beings without exception in the Self, and thus in Me.

explanations.en: Having known this, you will not be deluded again in this way. By this knowledge you will see all beings without exception in the Self, and then in Me. The vision of unity is the fruit of genuine knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि॥
verses.transliteration:

translations.english: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet shalt thou cross over all sin by the raft of wisdom.

explanations.en: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over all sin by the boat of knowledge alone. The absoluteness of the claim matches the absoluteness of knowledge: it overrides all past karma.

ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा॥

translations.english: As the burning fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so doth the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes.

explanations.en: As a fire reduces kindling to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all karma to ashes. Knowledge destroys even the residue of karma already accumulated.

verses.sanskrit:

तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति॥

translations.english: Verily there is no purifier in this world like wisdom; he that is perfected in yoga finds it in the Self in due season.

explanations.en: There is nothing as purifying as knowledge in this world. One who is perfected by yoga finds this within themselves in time. The finding is described as an interior discovery, not an external acquisition.

ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति॥

translations.english: The man who is full of faith obtaineth wisdom, and he also who hath mastery over his senses; and, having obtained wisdom, he goeth swiftly to the supreme Peace.

explanations.en: The person of faith obtains knowledge, having devoted himself to it and restrained his senses. Having obtained knowledge, he quickly attains supreme peace. Faith, effort, and sense-restraint together produce the result.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः॥

translations.english: But the ignorant, faithless, doubting self goeth to destruction; nor this world, nor that beyond, nor happiness, is there for the doubting self.

explanations.en: The ignorant person, the faithless person, and the doubting person perish. For the doubting person there is neither this world nor the next, nor any happiness. Doubt, unlike honest questioning, is a permanent suspension that prevents any action.

explanations.en: Actions do not bind one who has renounced all actions in yoga, who has cut doubt by knowledge, and who is established in the Self. O Dhanamjaya, actions do not bind such a person.

अर्जुन उवाच
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम्॥

translations.english: Arjuna said: Renunciation of actions Thou praisest, O Krishna, and then also yoga. Of the two which one is the better? That tell me conclusively.

explanations.en: Arjuna asks Krishna to give him a definitive answer: is renunciation of action better, or is action itself the path? Both have been praised and he is genuinely confused about which to practice.

संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते॥

translations.english: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and yoga by action both lead to the highest bliss; of the two, yoga by action is verily better than renunciation of action.

explanations.en: Krishna answers that both renunciation and karma yoga lead to the highest good, but karma yoga is superior to renunciation of action. The distinction matters because Arjuna is a warrior, not a monk.

verses.sanskrit:
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।
अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः॥
verses.transliteration:
nādatte kasyacitpāpaṁ na caiva sukṛtaṁ vibhuḥ
ajñānenāvṛtaṁ jñānaṁ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ

translations.english: The Lord accepteth neither the evil-doing nor yet the well-doing of any. Wisdom is enveloped by unwisdom; therewith mortals are deluded.

explanations.en: The All-pervading One does not receive the sin or merit of anyone. Knowledge is covered by ignorance and thereby beings are deluded. Sin and merit belong to the world of conditioned beings, not to Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:

तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्॥

translations.english: Verily, in whom unwisdom is destroyed by the wisdom of the Self, in them wisdom, shining as the sun, reveals the Supreme.

explanations.en: But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the Self, that knowledge illuminates the Supreme like the sun. When ignorance is removed, the Self reveals itself without any additional effort.

verses.sanskrit:
इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः॥
verses.transliteration:
ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṁ sāmye sthitaṁ manaḥ
nirdoṣaṁ hi samaṁ brahma tasmādbrahmaṇi te sthitāḥ

translations.english: Even here on earth everything is overcome by those whose mind remains balanced; the Eternal is incorruptible and balanced; therefore they are established in the Eternal.

explanations.en: Even here in this world those whose mind rests in equality have overcome the cycle of birth. Brahman is without flaw and equal; therefore they abide in Brahman. The equality of mind is not the cause but the expression of abiding in Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः॥

translations.english: The delights that are contact-born, they are verily wombs of pain, for they have beginning and ending, O Kaunteya; not in them may rejoice the wise.

explanations.en: The pleasures that are born of external contact are sources of sorrow. They have a beginning and an end. The wise do not rejoice in them. The observation is empirical: pleasures tied to conditions always end.

verses.sanskrit:

जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत्॥

jīvabhūtāṁ mahābāho yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat

translations.english: This the inferior. Know My other nature, the higher, the life-element, O mighty-armed, by which the universe is upheld.

explanations.en: This is the lower nature. But different from it is the higher nature (para prakriti) by which this world is sustained: the Jiva, the living principle. The distinction between matter and the life-principle it sustains is the pivot of this teaching.

verses.sanskrit:

अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा॥

translations.english: Know this to be the womb of all beings. I am the source of the forthgoing of the whole universe and likewise the place of its dissolving.

explanations.en: Know that all beings have their origin in these two natures. Krishna is the origin and dissolution of the entire universe. The two natures together constitute all of manifest existence.

verses.sanskrit:

मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव॥

translations.english: There is naught whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is threaded on Me, as rows of pearls on a string.

explanations.en: Nothing exists higher than Krishna. Everything is strung on Him as clusters of gems on a thread. The image of the thread running through all gems captures both the unity and the distinct existence of each thing.

translations.english: I the sapidity in waters, O son of Kuntî, I the radiance in moon and sun; the Word of Power in all the Vedas, sound in ether, and virility in men;

explanations.en: Krishna is the taste in water, the light of the moon and sun, the sacred syllable Om in the Vedas, the sound in ether, and the manhood in men. He is the subtle presence in each element that makes it what it is.

explanations.en: Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the wisdom of the wise, the splendor of the splendid. The seed metaphor points to the original generative principle behind all manifest forms.

explanations.en: Krishna is the strength of the strong that is free from desire and passion. He is the desire in beings that is not contrary to dharma. Strength and desire are not wrong in themselves; only their misuse is wrong.

verses.sanskrit:

मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि॥

explanations.en: And the states of sattva, rajas, and tamas are from Me alone. But I am not in them; they are in Me. The gunas arise from Krishna but do not contain or define him.

translations.english: Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again.

explanations.en: And remembering again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, great is my wonder, O king. I rejoice again and again. Sanjaya's response is not intellectual but experiential: wonder and joy, again and again.

verses.transliteration:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama18.78

translations.english: Wherever is Krishna, Yoga's Lord, wherever is Pârtha, the archer, assured are there prosperity, victory and happiness. So I think.

explanations.en: Wherever there is Krishna the Lord of yoga, and wherever there is Arjuna the great bowman, there is prosperity, victory, happiness, and firm resolve: this is my view. The Gita closes with Sanjaya's prophecy: the union of the divine and the human is the basis of all true flourishing.
